records.productName: SPRINT STANDARD Black & White Film Developer
records.preparation: Dilute concentrate 1+9 with water to make working solution.
records.reuseInstructions: Sprint's basic negative-processing directions use the developer once only. For larger quantities, Sprint also documents replenished processing.
records.capacityText: 1 litre concentrate makes 10 litres working solution, enough for at least 50 rolls of 35mm 36-exposure film; replenished solution from 1 litre concentrate is stated as enough for about 110 rolls.
records.sourceTitle: Sprint Systems - How To Mix STANDARD Black & White Film Developer

records.preparation: Shake the concentrate vigorously and prepare immediately before use by diluting 1+4 with water.
records.capacityText: Use at least 250 ml working solution per film.
records.shelfLifeOpened: Concentrated developer can be used for 9 months after opening.

records.preparation: Mix Solution A and Solution B with water at standard dilution 1+2+100. The standard kits provide 250 ml A and 500 ml B and can make 25 litres working solution.
records.capacityText: Up to 1000 square centimetres of film per litre working solution: 2 rolls 135-36, 2 rolls 120, 1 roll 220, 8 sheets 4x5 or 2 sheets 8x10.
records.shelfLifeOpened: Both component solutions are stated to keep up to 10 years, even in half-filled bottles.
records.shelfLifeWorking: Prepared working solution keeps for about one hour in open containers without affecting development quality.

records.manufacturer: SPUR Photochemie Dr. Heidrich und Schain GbR
records.preparation: Dilute the concentrate with water according to the film and desired image characteristics; SPUR documents a broad dilution range, commonly 1+50 to 1+200.
records.capacityText: At 1+50, 250 ml concentrate yields 50 film developments; at 1+100, 250 ml concentrate yields 100 film developments.
records.shelfLifeUnopened: Sealed original bottle: at least 4-5 years. Do not refrigerate because of precipitation risk.
records.sourceTitle: SPUR ACUROL-N Data Sheet and manufacturer technical article

records.manufacturer: SPUR Photochemie Dr. Heidrich und Schain GbR
records.preparation: Mix Parts A and B in equal amounts to prepare the working solution, then dilute with water according to the development chart.
records.capacityText: For one 35mm film, the manufacturer specifies approximately 8-10 ml minimum total concentrate; higher working-solution volume may be required at stronger dilutions.
records.shelfLifeUnopened: Part A in unopened original bottle: at least 2.5 years when stored cool; Part B has virtually unlimited shelf life.
records.storageNotes: After opening Part A, SPUR recommends protective gas. Part B does not require protective gas.

records.manufacturer: SPUR Photochemie Dr. Heidrich und Schain GbR
records.preparation: Compound the working solution from Part A and Part B according to the dilution specified in the SPUR development chart; it is a two-component developer, not a two-bath process.
records.shelfLifeUnopened: Part A unopened: approximately 2.5-3 years when stored relatively cool, but not below about 10-12 C. Part B has almost unlimited shelf life.
records.storageNotes: SPUR recommends protective gas for opened Part A bottles to extend shelf life.

records.manufacturer: SPUR Photochemie Dr. Heidrich und Schain GbR
records.preparation: Mix Part A and Part B in equal parts to make the working solution, then follow the film-specific development chart.
records.shelfLifeUnopened: Part A unopened: at least 2 years when stored relatively cool, but not refrigerated. Part B has almost unlimited shelf life.
records.shelfLifeWorking: Prepared working solution is not very durable and should be used within the next hours after preparation.

records.manufacturer: SPUR Photochemie Dr. Heidrich und Schain GbR
records.preparation: Use Part A at the film-specific dilution and add Part B in the X, Y, Z or 0 proportion defined by SPUR. For example, 1+14/Z in 500 ml uses about 33 ml Part A plus 50 ml Part B and water to 500 ml.
records.storageNotes: SPUR recommends distilled water for the working solutions used with SHADOWmax.

records.manufacturer: SPUR Photochemie Dr. Heidrich und Schain GbR
records.preparation: Dilute the concentrate according to the film-development chart; for paper the standard dilution is 1+20.
records.capacityText: For film, 250 ml concentrate develops about 30 35mm or roll films on average. For paper at 1+20, one litre working solution develops about 40 18x24 cm RC prints.
records.sourceTitle: SPUR UFP Universal Developer manufacturer information

records.preparation: Dilute the concentrate 1+15 or 1+31 with water for amateur processing; the professional package documents 1+15.
records.sourceTitle: Bellini Foto HYDROFEN Technical Data Sheet

records.capacityText: A 500 ml bottle of concentrate makes 16 litres ready-to-use developer at dilution B (1+31).
records.sourceTitle: Bellini Foto EURO HC Film Developer

records.preparation: Dilute concentrate 1+1 with water. A 500 ml bottle prepares 1 litre ready-to-use developer.
records.sourceTitle: Bellini Foto ECOFILM Technical Data Sheet
